```{r}
Q1 = read.csv("AHSnpa11bp.csv")
```

# Question 1:

The question: **How does diet modify the relationship between the risk of type 2 diabetes and risks of obesity within Australians aged 18-64, after accounting for age, sex, physical activity levels?**

```{r}
#Cleaning of Q1A
#Accounting for the ranges of every variable
Q1$AGDBBC[Q1$AGDBBC == 99] = NA
Q1$BMISC[Q1$BMISC %in% c(0, 98, 99)] = NA
Q1$EXLWMBC[Q1$EXLWMBC %in% c(9996, 9998, 9999)] = NA
Q1$EXLWVBC[Q1$EXLWVBC %in% c(9996, 9998, 9999)] = NA
#Removing if Pregnant
Q1$FEMLSBC[Q1$FEMLSBC == 2] = NA
#Removing if under the age of 25
Q1$AGEC[Q1$AGEC < 25] = NA

Q1A = data.frame(
  BMI = Q1$BMISC, #Obeseity variable
    Diabetes = ifelse(Q1$AGDBBC == 97, "No diabetes",
                    ifelse(Q1$AGDBBC == 1, "Type 1",
                           ifelse(Q1$AGDBBC >= 2, "Type 2", NA))),
  Carbs = (Q1$CHOPER1 + Q1$CHOPER2)/2, #Percentage of energy
  Fat = (Q1$SATPER1 + Q1$SATPER2)/2, #Percentage of energy
  SodiumIntake = (Q1$SODIUMT1 + Q1$SODIUMT2)/4000, #mg
  Sugar = (16*(Q1$ADDSUG1N + Q1$ADDSUG2N)/2)/(Q1$ENERGYF1 + Q1$ENRGYF1 + Q1$ENERGYF2 + Q1$ENRGYF2)/2, 
  #Confounding variables
  Age = Q1$AGEC, #2 to 85
  Sex = ifelse(Q1$SEX == 1, "Male", "Female"), #1 = Male, 2 = Female
  PhysicalActivity = Q1$EXLWMBC + 2 * Q1$EXLWVBC, #moderate + 2*Vigorous
  Energy = (Q1$ENERGYF1 + Q1$ENRGYF1 + Q1$ENERGYF2 + Q1$ENRGYF2)/2 #Continuous 0 - 99999(kJ)
)
Q1A = na.omit(Q1A)
  
```

# Summary of Statistics

Total Number of Variables:

```{r}
nrow(Q1A)
```

The response variable is obesity using the BMI. Where a participant is recorded as obese if BMI is greater than 30. This is roughly 25% of the data.

```{r}
summary(Q1A$BMI)

```

The predictor variables are diabetes type, measured through the age of diagnosis (25 and above = type 2), and different diet statistics including Carb % of energy, Fat % of energy, Sodium intake in mg and Sugar % of Energy

```{r}
prop.table(table(Q1A$Diabetes, useNA = "ifany"))
summary(Q1A[, c("Carbs", "Fat", "SodiumIntake", "Sugar")])
```

The confounding variables are Age, Sex, Physical Activity levels and Total Energy

```{r}
prop.table(table(Q1A$Sex, useNA = "ifany"))
summary(Q1A[, c("Age", "PhysicalActivity", "Energy")])
```

## Distribution of BMI

```{r}
h = hist(Q1A$BMI,
          breaks = 20,
          plot = FALSE)

cols = ifelse(h$mids < 30, "lightgreen", "lightcoral")

plot(h,
     col = cols,
     main = "Distribution of BMI",
     xlab = "BMI")

abline(v = 30, lty = 2, lwd = 3)
```

The data is positively skewed, which is expected from the summary given above.

## Comparison between BMI and Diabetes

```{r}
boxplot(BMI ~ Diabetes, data = Q1A,
        main = "BMI by Diabetes Status",
        xlab = "Diabetes Status",
        ylab = "BMI",
        col = c("lightgreen", "lightblue", "lightcoral"))

```

## Comparison of diet variables to BMI

```{r}
# Colours for diabetes groups
cols <- c(
  "No diabetes" = "lightgreen",
  "Type 1" = "blue",
  "Type 2" = "red"
)

# BMI vs Carbohydrate
plot(Q1A$Carbs, Q1A$BMI,
     col = adjustcolor(cols[Q1A$Diabetes], alpha.f = 0.3),
     pch = 19, cex = 0.5,
     main = "BMI vs Carbohydrate",
     xlab = "Carbohydrate (% energy)",
     ylab = "BMI")

abline(lm(BMI ~ Carbs, data = Q1A[Q1A$Diabetes == "No diabetes", ]),
       col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2)
abline(lm(BMI ~ Carbs, data = Q1A[Q1A$Diabetes == "Type 1", ]),
       col = "navy", lwd = 2)
abline(lm(BMI ~ Carbs, data = Q1A[Q1A$Diabetes == "Type 2", ]),
       col = "darkred", lwd = 2)

legend("topright",
       legend = c("No diabetes", "Type 1", "Type 2"),
       col = c("darkgreen", "navy", "darkred"),
       lwd = 2, bty = "n")


# BMI vs Saturated Fat
plot(Q1A$Fat, Q1A$BMI,
     col = adjustcolor(cols[Q1A$Diabetes], alpha.f = 0.3),
     pch = 19, cex = 0.5,
     main = "BMI vs Saturated Fat",
     xlab = "Saturated fat (% energy)",
     ylab = "BMI")

abline(lm(BMI ~ Fat, data = Q1A[Q1A$Diabetes == "No diabetes", ]),
       col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2)
abline(lm(BMI ~ Fat, data = Q1A[Q1A$Diabetes == "Type 1", ]),
       col = "navy", lwd = 2)
abline(lm(BMI ~ Fat, data = Q1A[Q1A$Diabetes == "Type 2", ]),
       col = "darkred", lwd = 2)

legend("topright",
       legend = c("No diabetes", "Type 1", "Type 2"),
       col = c("darkgreen", "navy", "darkred"),
       lwd = 2, bty = "n")


# BMI vs Sodium
plot(Q1A$SodiumIntake, Q1A$BMI,
     col = adjustcolor(cols[Q1A$Diabetes], alpha.f = 0.3),
     pch = 19, cex = 0.5,
     main = "BMI vs Sodium",
     xlab = "Sodium intake",
     ylab = "BMI")

abline(lm(BMI ~ SodiumIntake, data = Q1A[Q1A$Diabetes == "No diabetes", ]),
       col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2)
abline(lm(BMI ~ SodiumIntake, data = Q1A[Q1A$Diabetes == "Type 1", ]),
       col = "navy", lwd = 2)
abline(lm(BMI ~ SodiumIntake, data = Q1A[Q1A$Diabetes == "Type 2", ]),
       col = "darkred", lwd = 2)

legend("topright",
       legend = c("No diabetes", "Type 1", "Type 2"),
       col = c("darkgreen", "navy", "darkred"),
       lwd = 2, bty = "n")


# BMI vs Added Sugar
plot(Q1A$Sugar, Q1A$BMI,
     col = adjustcolor(cols[Q1A$Diabetes], alpha.f = 0.3),
     pch = 19, cex = 0.5,
     main = "BMI vs Added Sugar",
     xlab = "Added sugar",
     ylab = "BMI")

abline(lm(BMI ~ Sugar, data = Q1A[Q1A$Diabetes == "No diabetes", ]),
       col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2)
abline(lm(BMI ~ Sugar, data = Q1A[Q1A$Diabetes == "Type 1", ]),
       col = "navy", lwd = 2)
abline(lm(BMI ~ Sugar, data = Q1A[Q1A$Diabetes == "Type 2", ]),
       col = "darkred", lwd = 2)

legend("topright",
       legend = c("No diabetes", "Type 1", "Type 2"),
       col = c("darkgreen", "navy", "darkred"),
       lwd = 2, bty = "n")
```

Based on the analysis, is seems that Sodium and Saturated Fat may have the biggest interaction effect on people with type 2 Diabetes
